title: Gynaecological Procedures
body: The mucosal lining of the female genitalia is extremely sensitive to pain. The nerve innervation of the cervix is also different to that of the body of the uterus.
instruction: Select Continue to open the remaining text.

_next.ariaLabel: Select here to move to the next.

_items.body: Nerve endings are more abundant in the cervix particularly the internal os than in the body of uterus.

Pain transmission from the uterus and cervix occur along two different pathways:
  • Sensory fibres from uterus go through T11 and T12 nerve roots to the central nervous system
  • Sensory fibres of the cervix go through the 2nd, 3rd and 4th sacral nerves

EMLA is thought to block nerve conduction at the 2<sup>nd</sup>, 3<sup>rd</sup> and 4<sup>th</sup> sacral nerves when applied to the genital mucosa of the cervix. After application, EMLA is rapidly absorbed, and the onset of action is 5 to 10 minutes.

body: There are several procedures in which the use of EMLA would be beneficial and reduce the pain associated with the procedure.

An intrauterine device provides reliable, effective and long-term contraception. However, insertion of the device is associated with a certain degree of pain, which deters women from selecting this type of contraception.

title: Insertion of Intrauterine Device (IUD)
body: The pain associated with insertion can be due to different steps in the insertion process:
instruction: Select each checkmark on the picture to read more.
mobileInstruction: Select each checkmark to read more.
_comment: setCompletionOn = inview | allItems

_items.body:
• Application of the tenaculum on the cervical lip can induce severe pain.
  • Insertion of sound (to measure uterine depth) and insertion of the intrauterine device inserter tube and placement of the intrauterine device inside the uterine cavity can add to pain perception
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

body:
Intrauterine device insertion is painful for 50% or more of women who have the procedure. Pain can range from average to severe, with the addition of cramping, malaise and nausea in some patients.

There are certain factors which can aggravate the pain of intrauterine device insertion, including:

_items.text: Nulliparity
Long interval with pregnancy or last menstruation

body: If the pain is not relieved, it can increase the risk of vasovagal shock and cardiac arrhythmias.

There is no agreement on the most effective intervention to decrease pain associated with intrauterine device insertion.

Different pain methods have been used prior to insertion including oral ibuprofen, diclofenac, nitroprusside and local anaesthetics such as lidocaine and prostaglandin.
Studies show that the application of EMLA cream to the cervix prior to insertion of the intrauterine device reduces and alleviates pain.
instruction: Select the pictures below to read more.

_items.backBody:
EMLA cream is rapidly absorbed. When applied to the mucous membranes it is rapidly absorbed (5 to 7 minutes) compared to absorption via the skin (approximately 1 hour).

The optimal time therefore for the application of EMLA cream is 5 to 10 minutes.

EMLA has a favourable safety profile with rare side effects. These adverse effects may include:
  • Local skin reactions
  • Bradycardia
  • Burning sensation
  • Pruritus
  • Erythema

title: Speculum examinations in postmenopausal women
body: The female genital mucosa is sensitive to pain, which is increased when there is atrophy or inflammation.
instruction: Select Continue to open the remaining text.

_next.ariaLabel: Select here to move to the next.

_items.body: After menopause oestrogen levels decrease which leads to several adverse vaginal symptoms including dryness, loss of tone, irritation, hyperalgesia and pain. These symptoms may be exacerbated during sexual intercourse or vaginal examination.

A speculum is used during vaginal examination, and insertion of the speculum can be painful and provoke anxiety in post-menopausal women. Different topical anaesthetics have been used to help reduce the pain including EMLA, benzocaine gel, lidocaine gel and Mepivacaine.

Studies show that the application of EMLA cream to the genital mucosa prior to vaginal examination greatly reduces pain of speculum insertion. Pain is decreased on insertion, dilation and extraction of the speculum.

_graphic.attribution: A speculum is used to widen the vaginal walls during examination

body: Hysterosalpingography is an x-ray procedure that is used to visualise the uterus and fallopian tubes. It is often used to determine if the fallopian tubes are blocked or if the inside of the uterus is of normal size and shape. These are factors which could contribute to infertility.

title: Hysterosalpingography (HSG)
instruction: Select each checkmark on the picture to read more.
mobileInstruction: Select each checkmark to read more.
_comment: setCompletionOn = inview | allItems

_items.body: Hysterosalpingography requires the insertion of a contrast medium into the uterus and fallopian tubes.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

_items.body: The contrast medium will show up on x-ray and outline the inner shape and size of the uterus as well as the fallopian tubes.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

_items.body: Hysterosalpingography is a painful procedure but is also a necessary tool in evaluating infertility. 85% of patients who have this procedure report that it is painful and 50% say that the pain is moderate to severe.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

body:
To reduce the pain intravenous opioid medication was given. However, this requires special care as IV narcotics are being used and there is an associated cost. This makes this pain relief method unfeasible.

The insertion of lidocaine and prilocaine into the uterus prior to the procedure was also found to be ineffective.
Studies showed that the application of EMLA cream to the cervix prior to hysterosalpingography significantly reduced the pain of the procedure.
instruction: Select Continue to open the remaining text.

_items.body: Cervical instrumentation is considered the most painful step of the procedure and EMLA reduced the pain perception during this step.
Further to these studies it was shown that EMLA, by providing pain relief during the procedure, had an impact on long-term pain perception.

title: Genital Procedures
body: Male circumcision is a very common surgical procedure, with approximately 30% of males being circumcised worldwide.

title: Circumcision
body: There are several medical benefits of newborn male circumcision:
instruction: Drag the circle along the horizontal line to reveal more information.

_items.title: Item 1
_items.body: Decrease in infant urinary tract infections.

_items.title: Item 2
_items.body: Immediate protection against inflammatory penile skin conditions such as balanitis, posthitis and balanoposthitis.

_items.title: Item 3
_items.body: Future protection against penile cancer, human papillomavirus, herpes simplex virus type 2, human immunodeficiency virus and sexually transmitted diseases.

body:
Circumcision is a painful procedure, and newborns that undergo circumcision show a strong endogenous reaction and high intensity pain response.

These responses are measurable in the increased heart and respiratory rate and transcutaneous oxygen saturation seen during circumcision. Babies also cry during the procedure and can be irritable and feed poorly afterwards.

The application of EMLA cream prior to circumcision reduced the infant response to pain more so than with oral sucrose alone (another management technique used during circumcision).

There was also less of an increase in heart rate and oxygen saturation with EMLA than with oral sucrose.

The use of EMLA and oral sucrose together during circumcision provided better results than EMLA used alone.

body:
Human papillomavirus infections are the most prevalent sexually transmitted viral disease. Human papillomavirus causes warts.

Some types of the virus cause skin warts and others cause anogenital warts. There are over 100 known types of human papillomavirus.

Some types only infect the skin and mucosa of the anogenital region.

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Lesions
body: Some characteristics of genital warts include:
instruction: Select the picture below until you have seen all the information.

_items.body: Anogenital warts (also known as genital warts, condylomata acuminata, condylomas) are benign proliferative lesions caused by human papillomavirus types 6 and 11, which are found in >95% of lesions.
Anogenital warts are often co-infected with ‘high risk’ human papillomaviruses such as human papillomavirus 16.
Genital warts are sexually transmitted, with transmission rates of ~60% between partners.
Genital warts are more common among immunocompromised patients. Pregnancy, immunosuppression, or maceration of the skin may accelerate the growth and spread of warts.

body:
In males, warts occur most commonly under the foreskin, on the coronal sulcus, within the urethral meatus, and on the penile shaft. They may occur around the anus and in the rectum.

In females the warts occur most commonly on the vulva, vaginal wall, cervix and perineum. The urethra and anal region may be affected.

European Guidelines recommend the use of local anaesthetic cream when treating / removing human papillomavirus lesions. The treatment options include:
  • Electrosurgery
  • Curettage
  • Scissors excision
  • Laser therapy

Surgery may be used as the primary treatment method, with many patients being treated under local anaesthetic. It is recommended that local anaesthetic cream be used before infiltration anaesthesia to significantly reduce the discomfort from injections.

Cryotherapy can be used to removal genital warts. However, this is a painful procedure. The use of intralesional injection of lidocaine to reduce pain is compromised because the infiltration itself is painful. With insufficient pain relief cryotherapy may not be carried out thoroughly, allowing for lesions to remain and regrowth to occur.
instruction: Select each checkmark on the picture to read more.
mobileInstruction: Select each checkmark to read more.
_comment: setCompletionOn = inview | allItems

_items.body:
Using EMLA prior to any lidocaine infiltration reduces the pain of infiltration. The application of cream is associated with little to no pain.

Studies show that pre-treatment with EMLA lead to 65% of patients not experiencing any pain during cryotherapy. Including EMLA in the treatment protocol means that more complete freezing of genital warts is possible, and the patient will be more cooperative.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

_items.body: The prior use of EMLA with occlusive dressing also allows for the procedure to be completed more timeously because the patient is not in any pain.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

body: CO<sub>2</sub> Laser therapy is another surgical treatment option for the removal of genital warts. This treatment method has minimal tissue aggression and there is no scarring, like there is with conventional therapy.

_items.body: Prior to laser therapy the injection of a local anaesthetic into the treatment area is necessary. This is often a painful procedure that can cause bleeding, which in turn hinders penetration of the laser beam and so reduces treatment efficacy.
The application of EMLA cream for 3 to 5 minutes provides adequate anaesthesia for the treatment to be administered without discomfort to the patient and disturbance for the surgeon.

EMLA cream does provide a weaker anaesthetic effect over extensive lesion areas than smaller lesions areas, irrespective of the localisation in extra- or intra-cervical sites. Also, anaesthesia of extra-cervical sites is more effective than that of the uterine cervix.

title: Venous Ulcer Debridement
body:
Venous leg ulcers are chronic wounds that are caused by prolonged venous insufficiency. These ulcers develop because of poor blood flow in the veins, leading to tissue breakdown. This primarily affects the lower extremities. Over time patients may develop infections and experience delayed healing and disability.

Venous ulcer – before and after surgical debridement

There is no specific staging instrument for venous leg ulcers, but the clinical, etiology, anatomy, physiology (CEAP) classification is often used in patients with chronic venous insufficiency.

CEAP Classification

Patients with chronic leg ulceration have several difficulties associated with living with chronic ulceration including:
  • Frequent experience of moderate to severe wound pain
  • Pain may not be alleviated with use of oral analgesics
  • Poorly controlled ulcer pain

title: Indications
body:
The consequences of the above problems are that timely and effective wound management techniques may not be implemented which in turn increases wound healing time and patients experience continuous pain which affects their quality of life.

This type of pain is referred to as wound related pain (WRP) and 85% of patients with leg ulcers experience this pain. WRP is a major limiting factor in their daily lives, and it reduces the patients’ ability to tolerate wound treatment. This reduces or delays wound healing.
instruction: Select the pictures below to read more.

_items.backBody: Thorough cleansing of leg ulcers is an essential part of treatment. Necrotic tissue is known to delay healing. Debridement of leg ulcers is an accepted and recommended practice to remove necrotic tissue, slough and fibrinous plaques. A clean ulcer promotes growth of granulation tissue and epithelialisation. It also reduces the risk of infection and odour from the wound. This promotes healing and enables skin grafting.

A clean leg ulcer can be achieved through enzymatic preparations or repeated wet dressings. However, in many cases mechanical debridement is necessary. Sharp debridement is the most efficient method for treating the wound bed and it is also a fast method for achieving a clean ulcer. The necrotic tissue, bacteria and foreign bodies cannot be removed as rapidly and as effectively by any other method.

body: Mechanical debridement often involves the use of a sharp curette or scissors to remove necrosis just above the level of viable tissue. This process may need to be repeated several times.
instruction: Select each checkmark on the picture to read more.
mobileInstruction: Select each checkmark to read more.

_items.body: The use of sharp debridement is often limited though because of the pain experienced by the patient.

_items.body: Wound cleaning may not be as radical as necessary, and many patients request that debridement be stopped before it can be completed because they are unable to tolerate the pain.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

_items.body: Patients may also experience pain for several hours after treatment.
_items._comment: Supported classes = 'hide-desktop-image' | 'hide-popup-image'. Additional classes can be used but they must be predefined in one of the Less files

body: EMLA can be used prior to debridement to provide effective pain relief from debridement of venous and arterial leg ulcers. EMLA also provides patients with pain relief at rest. This decreases the need for oral analgesia for pain management. The analgesic effect remained effective with successive treatments. EMLA also significantly reduces the frequency of post-cleansing pain. These factors most likely result in better wound cleaning and the faster appearance of clear ulcers.
instruction: Select Continue to open the remaining text.

_next.ariaLabel: Select here to move to the next.

_items.body:
Local analgesia with topically applied EMLA cream offers the majority of patients’ good pain relief. This allows for:
  • Satisfactory debridement of even chronic ulcers.
  • Fewer treatment visits.
  • Shortened treatment duration.
  • A systematic, standardised treatment.
EMLA is the only topical anaesthetic for which there is clinical evidence of analgesic efficacy in debridement.

EMLA has a favourable safety profile and is well tolerated.
  • No serious untoward events/ local reactions.
  • No statistically significant differences vs. controls in local reactions or adverse effects on:
    • Granulation tissue.
    • Ulcer area.
    • Bacterial flora.

body:
EMLA also has antibacterial and antiviral properties which are beneficial in wound healing.
  • Lidocaine had antibacterial and antiviral properties in concentration of 0,5 to 2%

body:
It is important to alleviate pain during venepuncture for several reasons, namely:
  • It is more humane
  • Avoids acute physiological instability associated with invasive interventions
    • Hypoxemia
    • Haemodynamic variations
  • Prevents long-term negative psychological effects later in life

Analgesia is therefore beneficial when doing venepuncture on children.

Several reasons for this include:

_items.body: • Gain children’s confidence and allows parents to remain with their child during the procedure.
• Reduces anxiety.
• Decreases the need for deeper sedation.

body:
The use of EMLA cream or patch substantially improves the ease of venepuncture in children. It also reduces the effort and distress associated with having to restrain a child during venepuncture.

EMLA also reduces the anxiety children experience when undergoing venepuncture and pain of the procedure itself.

Parents and caregivers rate the effectiveness of EMLA highly. In a study it was found that caregivers preferred the cream and found it to be effective in 97.8% of children.

As discussed, the benefits of using EMLA in venepuncture procedures in children include:

title: IV cannulation/skin needle insertion: Adults
body:
IV cannulation is one of the most commonly performed invasive in-hospital procedures.

This is generally painful irrespective of the cannula size or intradermal injection of local anaesthetic. This can lead to a higher incidence of vasovagal reactions and pressor reactions.

title: IV cannulation/skin needle insertion: Adults
body: Inadequate pain relief during IV cannulation can have several negative effects:
instruction: Select Continue to open the remaining text.

_next.ariaLabel: Select here to move to the next.

_items.body:
• Unpleasant for the patient
  • Increases anxiety regarding future treatments and may lead to treatment avoidance
  • May trigger autonomic response which results in vasoconstriction

• Make procedure more difficult
  • Increase the number of attempts required to insert cannula
  • Increase risk of infection and other complications

body:
The use of local injectable anaesthetics is not effective in reducing pain because the injection is into the dermis. This is also painful and may compound the effect of needle phobia. It also increases the possible risk of contaminated sharps and those associated dangers.

Therefore, it is important that pain be managed during IV cannulation, so as with children a topical anaesthetic is recommended.

title: Indications
body: There are several benefits associated with using a non-invasive and effective local anaesthetic:
instruction: Select the pictures below to read more.

_items.backBody:
• Reduces pain and discomfort
  • Reduces adverse effects of cannulation
  • Relieves anxiety and needle phobia
  • Allows procedure to be carried out more easily
EMLA patch reduces the pain of IV cannulation as well as the incidence of vasovagal side-effects from IV cannulation in adults.

Further benefits of EMLA for IV cannulation include:
  • Negligible local skin reactions
  • Application time does not limit feasibility in outpatient facility
  • EMLA cream can significantly reduce pain in 5 minutes

title: Molluscum Contagiosum
body: Treatment of molluscum contagiosum with a comedo extractor or a curette is widely used, although removal is usually painful.
instruction: Select the picture below until you have seen all the information.

_items.body: EMLA cream effectively prevented pain after all 3 application times (15, 30 or 60 minutes) and allowed for the satisfactory curettage of molluscum contagiosum in children.
91% of children who were given EMLA cream felt little to no pain compared to 54% of children who received a placebo. In addition, no general side effects or serious local reactions were noted.

title: Excisional Biopsy or Curettage with Electrosurgery
body:
Needle puncture and infiltration anaesthesia is generally required for minor cutaneous surgical procedures and may be associated with anxiety, fear, discomfort, and pain.

EMLA may provide an alternative means of delivering anaesthesia. EMLA cream and patch are equally effective, although the patch may be advantageous when a patient is applying EMLA at home prior to the procedure. Generally, no unexpected adverse effects are observed.

title: EMLA plus occlusive dressing
body:
For minor skin surgical procedures involving excisional biopsy or curettage with electrosurgery, EMLA (eutectic lidocaine/prilocaine 5%) cream (EMLA)/Tegaderm and patch formulations were equally effective.

The use of EMLA under occlusion with an occlusive dressing before a minor cutaneous surgical procedure is an important advance in non-invasive analgesia.

title: Laser Resurfacing
body: EMLA cream is the topical anaesthetic most commonly used by physicians performing dermatological surgery.
instruction: Select the picture below until you have seen all the information.

_items.body: EMLA can be combined with remifentanil-based sedation as an alternative to regional or general anaesthesia. This means that airway management is not necessary, intra and postoperative safety and comfort of the patient is ensured and there are minimal complication and rapid recoveries.

Therefore, this combination allows for the benefits of regional or general anaesthetic without some of the risks and complications. It provides adequate depth of anaesthesia during outpatient facial laser resurfacing without complications.

The majority of patients are successfully anaesthetised in this manner.

title: Contraindications
body:
Known hypersensitivity to lidocaine and/or prilocaine or local anaesthetics of the amide type or to any of the excipients.

Infants between 0 – 12 months receiving treatment with methaemoglobinaemia-inducing medicines, e.g., dapsone, local anaesthetics such as prilocaine and benzocaine, nitrates and sulphonamides.

_items.body: Patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, hereditary or idiopathic methaemoglobinaemia are more susceptible to active-substance-inducing signs of methaemoglobinaemia. In glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient patients the antidote methylene blue is ineffective at methaemoglobin reduction, and is capable of oxidising haemoglobin itself, and therefore methylene blue therapy cannot be given.
Due to insufficient data on absorption, EMLA should not be applied to open wounds with the exception of leg ulcers.
Due to the potentially enhanced absorption on newly shaven skin, it is important to adhere to the recommended dosage, area and time of application.

Care should be taken when applying EMLA to patients with atopic dermatitis. A shorter application time, 15 – 30 minutes, may be sufficient. Prior to curettage of mollusca in children with atopic dermatitis, an application time of 30 minutes is recommended.

Care should be taken not to allow EMLA to come in contact with the eyes as it may cause eye irritation. Also, the loss of protective reflexes may allow corneal irritation and potential abrasion. If eye contact occurs, immediately rinse the eye in water or sodium chloride solution and protect it until sensation returns.

EMLA should not be applied to an impaired tympanic membrane. Tests on laboratory animals have shown that EMLA Cream has an ototoxic effect when instilled into the middle ear. Animals with an intact tympanic membrane, however, show no abnormality when exposed to EMLA Cream in the external auditory canal.
Lidocaine and prilocaine have bactericidal and antiviral properties in concentrations above 0.5 – 2 %. For this reason, the results of intracutaneous injections of live vaccines should be monitored.
Patients treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs class III (e.g., amiodarone) should be under close surveillance and ECG monitoring considered, since cardiac effects may be additive.
EMLA Cream contains macrogolglycerol hydroxystearate, which may cause skin reactions.
Clinical trial data on the safety and efficacy of EMLA Patch use in dermal peels is limited and EMLA Patch should be used with caution in these cases.

EMLA patch:

title: Drug interactions
body:
• Prilocaine in high doses may cause an increase in the methaemoglobin level particularly in conjunction with methaemoglobin-inducing agents (e.g., sulphonamides, nitrofurantoin, phenytoin, phenobarbital). This list is not exhaustive.
  • With large doses of EMLA, consideration should be given to the risk of additional systemic toxicity in patients receiving other local anaesthetics or agents structurally related to local anaesthetics. The toxic effects are additive.
  • Drugs that reduce the clearance of lidocaine (e.g., cimetidine or beta blockers) may cause potentially toxic plasma concentrations when lidocaine is given in repeated high doses over a long period.
  • Specific interaction studies with lidocaine/prilocaine and anti-arrhythmic class III (e.g. amiodarone) have not been performed, but caution is advised.

title: Pregnancy and Lactation
body: Animal studies do not indicate direct or indirect harmful effects with respect to pregnancy, embryonal/foetal development, parturition or postnatal development.

title: Pregnancy
body:
In both animals and humans, lidocaine and prilocaine cross the placental barrier and may be absorbed by the foetal tissues. Safety in pregnancy and lactation has not been established, but topical application is associated with low systemic absorption. Caution should be exercised when used in pregnant women.

Animal studies do not indicate direct or indirect harmful effects with respect to pregnancy, embryonal/foetal development, parturition or postnatal development. Embryofoetal toxicity has been shown with subcutaneous/intramuscular administration of high doses of lidocaine or prilocaine, much exceeding the amount used in EMLA cream or patch.

No specific disturbance to the reproductive process has so far been reported, e.g., an increased incidence of malformation or other directly or indirectly harmful effects on the foetus.

title: Lactation
body: Lidocaine and, in all probability, prilocaine are excreted in breast milk, but in such small quantities that there is generally no risk of the child being affected at therapeutic dose levels. EMLA cream and patch can be used during breastfeeding, if necessary, but the patch must not be applied directly to the breast where ingestion by the infant could occur.
